newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria railway seeks duty free equipment imports.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria railway seeks duty free equipment imports.

text.p: Bulgaria's state railway said on Thursday it would seek a waiver of custom fees and value added tax on imported equipment purchased by restructuring credits from international lending institutions.

The railway's general director Angel Dimitrov said the company had borrowed $152 million from the World Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to carry out a restructuring programme.
He said deals for equipment supplies worth more than $50 million had been sealed so far and more contracts, worth $23.8 million, were expected to be signed by the end of the year.
Machines and equipment worth $1.7 million will be delivered by the end of the year, Dimitrov told a news conference.
In 1997 the company expects to receive equipment worth $72.4 million and in 1998 and 1999 it will total $78 million.

"In a letter to the finance minister we have asked for lifting of custom fees and VAT which will total some $775,000 this year, $32.6 million next year and $35 million in 1998 and 1999," Dimitrov said.
He added that the loans had been guaranteed by the Bulgarian government and under the agreement with the two banks Bulgaria must contribute another $130 million for the project.
The loans will be spent on restructuring the outdated railway, updating information systems, wagon refurbishment and improving the railway company's structure and financial state.
Dimitrov said the railway's stabilisation programme included closures of inefficient secondary railway lines.
Passenger fares will rise by 30 percent from December 1 and freight rates also by 30 percent from January 1, he said.

Dimitrov said a local court had registered a new joint venture between Italy's Eurofer Ltd and a plant producing sleepers for railway tracks and electric pylons in the Danube river port of Svistov. "At the end of May the plant will start the production of new modern railway tracks," Dimitrov said.
Negotiations are underway for the establishment of two more joint ventures, he said.

The railway plans to set up a joint venture between Austrian engineering firm VAE Eisenbahnsystems AG and a Sofia railway point plant. The third venture is expected to be between Swiss-Swedish firm ABB and a Sofia railway plant for automatic and telemechanic equipment, he said.
